findingDetails.title: layoutLinks paths escape the tree root unvalidated, and the relayout rollback now writes through them
findingDetails.scopeProof: the value reaches the filesystem through two call sites in the reviewed file (:2577, :6431), and assertSafeToPlan's field list at :2836 omits layoutLinks entirely
findingDetails.case: a manifest with layoutLinks [{path: '../../outside/link', target: '../overlays/framework/x'}] makes apply create a link outside the tree, and a failed relayout re-create it during rollback
findingDetails.claim: assertSafeToPlan claims to refuse a manifest whose paths escape their roots but never inspects layoutLinks[].path or layoutLinks[].replaces.path
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: searched for any containment check on layoutLinks in the engine and in the tests; the only layoutLinks fixture (overlay-engine-sync.test.cjs:398) uses an in-tree path and no test exercises an escaping one
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: the manifest is authored by the repository owner, who can already write anywhere, so the gap may be treated as out of the threat model

results.notes: D2 refusal enforced at the single setting reader and inherited by every command; the layoutLinks gap is a pre-existing manifest-validation hole, not a D2 violation
still read-only; live criteria scheduled for the traceability iteration

noveltyJustification: one new P2 (weight 1) against one carried P2 (weight 1) gives a weighted new share of 0.5; the security pass opened a manifest field the correctness pass did not touch, so the finding is new rather than a refinement

reviewDepthApplicability.reason: trust-boundary review of a path-writing engine
